item.title: Netanyahu says Israel expects war with Iran to last weeks, not days
item.description: In closed-door remarks to local leaders, PM says aiming to end war’s most intensive phase before Passover or reduce Iran’s launch capabilities enough to shift to emergency routine, warns regime change in Tehran cannot be imposed 'at the push of a button'

item.title: Israeli officials expect Iran war to last at least two more weeks, pessimistic about regime change
item.description: Initial optimism after launch of Operation Lion’s Roar gives way to frustration as Tehran’s regime remains stable; Israeli officials say conflict unlikely to end soon and stress only Trump will decide when fighting stops

item.title: Iran downs Israeli drones as fighter jets maneuver to evade air defenses near missile launch sites
item.description: Iran has shot down several Israeli drones during the war while surface-to-air missiles have also threatened fighter jets, forcing pilots to maneuver midair to avoid hits as the Israeli Air Force hunts missile launchers and works to curb Tehran’s attacks

item.title: The Christian village caught between Israel and Hezbollah — spared by the IDF
item.description: Residents of Rmeish near Israel’s border remain in their homes despite fighting, but Israeli military warns it will strike if Hezbollah operatives hide among displaced civilians seeking refuge there

item.title: Iranian exiles in Berlin urge Israel to keep fighting until Tehran’s ayatollah regime collapses
item.description: Exiles meeting Israel’s ambassador in Berlin say the war is not against Iran but against the ayatollah regime, urging Israel not to allow a US deal with Tehran and to continue fighting until the government changes

item.title: Israel says war with Iran and Hezbollah will last 'only a few weeks'
item.description: Finance Ministry lowered its economic growth forecast for 2026, with the economy now projected to grow 4.7% in 2026, down from a previous forecast of 5.2%

item.title: Ramadan loses its spirit across Israel's Arab communities as Iran war empties mosques and markets
item.description: Movement restrictions, fear of missile fire and a shortage of shelters have disrupted the holy month across Arab towns in Israel; businesses report heavy losses and mosques stand half empty as residents say the war has dampened celebrations
